rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Governing equation for "Kirchhoff's laws and their applications" — state with units, then use in one numerical.
Junction: I1 + I2 = I3
Loop: Σ E = Σ IR

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ state the rule without its limit → ✅ note when it applies / stops applying.  ·  ❌ no diagram → ✅ add one labelled figure / structured list.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Two cells in one loop oppose or add according to their arrows.  ·  A zero-current branch can be removed when you only want the remaining currents.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: An application starts with a circuit diagram and one arrow on every branch. At each junction write one current as the sum of the others so that the junction law is already built in.  ·  For two loops, walk each loop and write Σ E = Σ IR, or the equivalent sum of rises and drops equal to zero. The shared resistor carries the difference or the sum of the loop currents, matching the arrows.

rows.text: A balanced galvanometer carries → B  ·  A shared resistor carries → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: The two equations are linear. Eliminate one current by substitution. A negative result flips that arrow and is then used as a positive magnitude in later arithmetic.  ·  A Wheatstone bridge is an application. If the bridge is balanced, the galvanometer branch has zero current, and the loop equations collapse to the ratio condition P/Q = R/S.  ·  A potentiometer is another application: the working battery drives a long wire, and the balance length is the point where the loop containing the test cell has zero current.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Do not invent a new current for a branch you already expressed as a sum.  ·  The shared resistor does not carry each loop current separately at the same time.  ·  Balance means zero galvanometer current, not zero battery current.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: A negative current is kept, with its direction reversed.  ·  Write the shared current explicitly.  ·  State the direction with the answer.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Write Junction: I1 + I2 = I3 and say what each symbol means.  ·  Mark the known values, then substitute one step at a time.  ·  Finish with the number, the unit, and the direction when the quantity has one.
